correctness.rationale: TARGET route: universal claim is 'for every q=3 mod 4, q>=11, w=[x,y]^2 z^3 on PSL(2,q) misses U_q'. A single q in the family with |w^{-1}(u)|>=1 for u in U_q suffices to disprove it. Report provides q=11 with explicit SL(2,11) lifts X=[[4,0],[6,3]], Y=[[2,10],[10,1]], Z=[[2,10],[3,10]], U=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Auditor independently re-ran inputs/artifacts/verify_counterexample.py (VERIFY_OK) and manually recomputed: det(X)=det(Y)=det(Z)=1 mod 11; q=11 satisfies q%4==3 and q>=11; U has trace 2 and is not +/-I so valid nontrivial unipotent lift defining U_q per topic; with [x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}, [X,Y]=[[10,5],[0,10]], [X,Y]^2=[[1,1],[0,1]]=U, Z^3=[[-1,0],[0,-1]]=-I, w=C2*Z3=-U which equals U in PSL(2,11) under M~-M. All arithmetic is exact 2x2 mod-11, deterministic proof by witness, not experimental evidence. PSL identification is correct; possible splitting of unipotents in PSL(2,q) does not affect correctness because the witness hits the exact representative defining U_q. Boundary conditions checked; no inference gap.
